answer_body: Immigration law in the U.S. is complex and constantly evolving. Policies, processing standards, and enforcement priorities shift over time, especially under agencies like U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) and the immigration courts overseen by the Executive Office for Immigration Review. A lawyer with years of experience has already navigated these changes and knows how to adapt strategies accordingly.

One major advantage of experience is familiarity with case patterns. Whether it’s a visa application, green card process, asylum claim, or deportation defense, seasoned attorneys have handled cases similar to yours. They know what documentation tends to be scrutinized, what mistakes to avoid, and how to present your case in the strongest possible way.

Also, local experience in Chicago matters. Immigration lawyers who regularly practice in the area understand how local immigration courts operate, including tendencies of specific judges or procedural expectations. This kind of insight can shape how your case is prepared and argued.
